segments.text: In sixteen forty-two, Rembrandt completed a very large group portrait for the great hall of the arquebusiers, one of Amsterdam's civic militias. Paintings like this were common in the city. Members often appeared side by side, in rows, so that each face could be seen.

segments.text: In sixteen seventy-eight, Samuel van Hoogstraten, who had studied with Rembrandt, wrote about the painting in a book on art. He reported a criticism: that Rembrandt had cared more for the picture as a whole than for the portraits he had been asked to paint. Even so, he believed it would outlast all its rivals. And he added that he wished Rembrandt had put more light into it. So its deep shadows were noticed early. But Hoogstraten does not call it a night scene.
